attempts.sql: SELECT c.symbol_id, COUNT(m.symbol_id)::INTEGER AS method_count FROM code.symbols c JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname LIKE c.qualname || '.%' AND m.qualname NOT LIKE c.qualname || '.%.%' JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = c.file_id WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND f.is_test = FALSE GROUP BY c.symbol_id HAVING COUNT(m.symbol_id) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, c.symbol_id ASC

request:
Which classes in the non-test code define at least 20 methods directly in their own body? Count every method definition separately (a property getter and its setter count as two; inherited methods and methods of nested classes do not count). Return each class's symbol ID and its method count, largest count first, ties broken by symbol ID alphabetically.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), method_count (integer). Order the rows as the question asks.
explanation: Joins each class to methods in the same file whose qualname is the class qualname plus one dotted segment (direct methods only, excluding nested classes' methods), restricted to non-test files. Counts those methods per class, keeps classes with at least 20, and orders by count descending then symbol ID.
sql: SELECT c.symbol_id, COUNT(m.symbol_id)::INTEGER AS method_count FROM code.symbols c JOIN code.symbols m ON m.file_id = c.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname LIKE c.qualname || '.%' AND m.qualname NOT LIKE c.qualname || '.%.%' JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = c.file_id WHERE c.kind = 'class' AND f.is_test = FALSE GROUP BY c.symbol_id HAVING COUNT(m.symbol_id) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, c.symbol_id ASC
